description: Now (measured on the release build): 01 -> {:ok,1}; - -> {:ok,0}; 1. -> {:ok,1.0}; 1e -> {:ok,1.0}; 0.12345678901234567890, 5e-324, 1e400 and 99999999999999999999 raise ArithmeticError; 1.7976931348623157e308 -> ...153e308; 2.2250738585072014e-308 -> ...202e-308. OTP json:decode answers invalid_byte, unexpected_end x3, exact values, and unexpected_sequence for 1e400. Change: scan the grammar with no arithmetic; accumulate integers of up to 18 digits; a float's text goes to Float.parse (measured to round correctly on all of the above); Float.parse :error -> unexpected_sequence; an integer that does not fit 64 bits -> {:error, {:unexpected_sequence, offset, token}} (decision D1: fz has no bignums). Deletes fraction_digits, scale, apply_scale, pow10, negate. No dependencies. Proposal page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-json-garbage.html (approved 2026-11-14). Worktree ../fz-json, base bd3edae98.

comments.text: Measured on ../fz-json (bd3edae98 + change): fixture 01320 holds 45 number inputs, and all 45 match Elixir 1.19.4's JSON.decode (oracle) on interp, run and build. That covers the grammar errors (01, -01, -, 1., 1e, 1e+, 1E-, .5, +1, 00, [1,01], [1e], {"a":1.}, 1.5x, 1ex, -x), the exact floats at the double edges, and out-of-range floats as unexpected_sequence with Elixir's rewritten text (1E400 -> "1.0e400"). -0e0 -> 0.0 as in Elixir. Fixture 01321 pins D1: an integer past 64 bits is {:unexpected_sequence, offset, text}. Both fixtures fail on the base binary. Fixture block: 01080-01099 was marked free but is full (fz-348 / fz-rs7); fz-nml claims 01320-01339, and the table row is corrected.

title: A JSON number is checked by its syntax and converted from its text
